notes: Identity assessment: Scribd HTML transcription of an uploaded primary article, with matching article title, all four authors, DOI 10.1177/1948550617751583, journal volume 10(2), pages 257–265, and 2018 copyright/2019 issue. The Scribd AI-enhanced display title differs from the article title. The supplied text ends partway through printed p. 262; it does not contain the complete nine-page article. Figure 1 on printed p. 260 (article p. 4) is incompletely transcribed: path labels and isolated coefficients survive, but the race-to-critical-knowledge path coefficient and its significance cannot be assigned. No PDF supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. Both rows identify the same original target construct. Study 1 compares White and Black participants; Study 2 is a White-only intervention. The description admits the direct between-group critical historical knowledge comparison, whereas the p. 4/Figure 1 locator points to an unstandardized regression path within a mediated-moderation model. Candidates: Table 1 reality-attunement t = 2.66 and text d = .49; an alternative uncertainty-coding analysis prints t = 1.76, p = .080, d = .33. The Table 1 note literally prints **p < .001, identical to the *** threshold; this is preserved without correction as candidate evidence. No candidate test was selected by row order or numeric agreement; no metric was converted. Candidates only: 111 + 43 = 154 initially recruited participants; (111 - 1) + 43 = 153 participants for analyses involving identity relevance. One White exclusion applies only to analyses involving that measure. Initial group counts are not explicitly final critical-model group counts; target-model completeness and test correspondence remain unresolved. No N inferred from df. Only original n/es/p assigned. Unassigned records are placeholders. Nulls reflect unresolved correspondence, not established absence from the complete paper.
